Antipatris
an-TIP-uh-tris
proper noun / place
Named by Herod the Great after his father Antipater; a rebuilt city on the road from Jerusalem toward Caesarea, at the edge of the Plain of Sharon.

📖 Biblical Definition

Antipatris is the city to which the Roman soldiers brought Paul by night after the plot against his life in Jerusalem. Luke records that the escort, as commanded, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris, and on the morrow the horsemen went on with him to Caesarea while the foot soldiers returned. The place stands on the military road that linked the holy city to the coastal seat of Roman power. It was not a sanctuary of pilgrimage but a waypoint of empire, rebuilt and named by Herod for political honor. Yet in the narrative of Acts it becomes a marker of God’s protection. The same Lord who had stood by Paul and promised that he must bear witness at Rome ordered the night march, the cavalry, the fortress route, and the city that received him before dawn. Antipatris therefore teaches the church that providence is not abstract comfort. It has roads, miles, watches, and intermediate towns. When enemies swear an oath of murder, God may answer with a tribune, a letter, and a night ride to Antipatris under armed guard. The intermediate town is as much under decree as the final destination.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Herodian city on the Jerusalem–Caesarea road; the night stop of Paul’s military escort after the plot in Jerusalem.

expand to see more

ANTIPATRIS, a city rebuilt by Herod the Great and named for Antipater.

It stood on the road from Jerusalem down toward Caesarea Maritima.

Roman soldiers brought Paul there by night under armed guard.

From Antipatris the horsemen continued with him to Caesarea.

The place marks the LORD’s use of imperial roads to preserve His servant.

📖 Key Scripture

Act 23:31 — "Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris."

Act 23:23 — "And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;"

Act 23:24 — "And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor."

Act 23:11 — "And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Critics reduce Antipatris to a footnote of Herodian urbanism; Scripture sets it inside the LORD’s defense of the apostolic witness.

expand to see more

The modern habit is to read such names as archaeological garnish—interesting to the tourist, irrelevant to faith. That is unbelief dressed as sophistication. Antipatris is where the murder-oath of more than forty men met the greater oath of God’s promise. The night stop is not filler between speeches; it is the geography of preservation. When the church forgets that, she also forgets that God still rules roads, rulers, and escorts for the sake of the gospel.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. What must be recovered is the conviction that biblical geography is not scenery for myth, but the real theatre of the LORD’s providence, judgment, and grace. The places of Scripture stand as witnesses that God acts in history, among real peoples, on real soil, for the glory of His name.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Antipatris is the Herodian waypoint where Paul’s night escort paused between Jerusalem and Caesarea under God’s protecting hand.

expand to see more

Name — Herod’s city in honor of Antipater his father.

Road — military route from Jerusalem to Caesarea.

Acts 23 — Paul brought there by night with soldiers.

Protection — the plot of the Jews cannot overthrow God’s word.

Providence — empire’s logistics serve the gospel’s advance.

Usage

"The soldiers brought Paul by night to Antipatris after the conspiracy in Jerusalem."

"Antipatris sat on the road that led down to Caesarea and the sea."

"The night stop declares that God keeps His promise to send Paul to Rome."
